ADDITIONAL SAFETY INFORMATION
UNSECURED BAGGAGE IS
A SAFETY RISK
All carry on baggage including passengers
personal effects shall be stowed either in
the overhead lockers or under the seat in
front of you. Do not stow it under your
feet in the exit rows. Unsecured baggage
can turn into a lethal missile in an accident
or severe turbulence. In the event of an
emergency evacuation, leave everything
behind. The number one priority is to
evacuate as quickly as possible. Taking
carry on baggage will slow down the
evacuation time on the slides and can
cause injury. If cabin baggage exceeds the
allowed size or weight, it must be checked
with your other baggage and not carried
in the aircraft cabin.
INTOXICATION AND
DISORDERLY BEHAVIOUR
The cabin atmosphere is pressurised to
about 8000ft above sea level, so any
alcohol you consume will have a
greater effect on you than normal.
It is against Civil Aviation Regulations
to enter an aircraft while in a state
of intoxication or to behave in an
offensive and disorderly manner while
in an aircraft.
JUMP AND SIT ONTO THE
EVACUATION SLIDE
Inflatable escape slides are found at all
doors and all over-wing exits. See the
diagram in the centre section of this card
which shows the exits on this aircraft.
When using an escape slide, fold your
arms across your chest and JUMP onto
the slide, and then sit with your feet and
legs together. Do not use your arms to
slow you down as this could result in
painful burns. Sit upright and look at
where you are going. Once you have
reached the ground, immediately move
away from the aircraft.
FLAT LEATHER SHOES ARE BEST
Leather shoes with flat heels are best in an
emergency. Always keep them on for take
off and landing. If you are required to
leave the aircraft, in an emergency, your
shoes will provide protection for your feet
when you are outside the aircraft. Do not
wear high heeled shoes as they can hinder
your movement over uneven surtaces and
can also puncture an evacuation slide. If
you do wear high heels, take them off
when instructed by the crew prior to going
down the escape slide.
AUTHORITY OF THE CREW
Passengers are reminded that the captain
is responsible for the maintenance of
discipline by all persons onboard.
Passengers must not obstruct or impede
anyone from exercising a power or
performing a duty that has been
conferred to them by or under the Civil
Aviation Regulations.
'BRACE' POSITION FOR IMPACT
The 'BRACE' position is designed to limit
the impact of forces on your body and
to help you survive an impact. Push your
lower back firmly into the back of your seat
with your seat belt fastened low and tight
over your hips. If you can reach the seat in
front, fold your arms together, place your
folded arms against the seat back in front
and rest your head on your arms. Place
your feet firmly on the floor. If you cannot
reach the seat in front, place your chest on
your lap with your head down. Clasp your
hands around your shins and place your
feet firmly on the ground. Take the time
and see which 'BRACE' position shown on
the front of the card is most suitable for
you in the seat in which you are sitting.
If the crew calls 'heads down, stay
down', adopt the 'BRACE' position
immediately and stay in the 'BRACE'
position until the aircraft stops
completely. Be aware there may be
more than one impact
SPEAK UP IF YOU SEE SOMETHING
OUT OF THE ORDINARY
Don't be reluctant to report
something that you think may be a
problem or something out of the
ordinary. Passengers' actions in alerting
crew can and have been known to
prevent accidents.
NO SMOKING
Smoking, especially in the toilet creates
an enormous fire hazard. To combat
this, smoke detectors have been fitted
in every toilet. Smoking is prohibited
on all Qantas aircraft. Heavy penalties
apply for non compliance. Fire remains
one of the greatest dangers to aircraft
safety. Ensure that lighters or safety
matches are kept in your pocket at all
times. In checked or carry on baggage
they may catch fire undetected.
RESTRICTIONS ON THE USE OF ELECTRONIC DEVICES
Electronic devices may affect the operation of the aircraft
instruments and systems. Please observe the restrictions listed below.

onboard the aircraft. Devices

and must be switched off
immediately the aircraft starts

Cellular telephones, transceivers,

Video cameras*, video players,

Hearing Aids; pacemakers,
